newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up at third straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up at third straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks roared ahead to reach a record high for the third consecutive day as the bolsa rallied on continuing success in Venezuela's on-going oil field auctions, traders said.
"The market today was the same as it has been over the past two days ... and it looks as though it's going to continue that way," Vencred broker Geronimo Paolini said.

Venezuela sold operating contracts to only three of the four fields offered Thursday, although one bid by Britain's Lasmo hit a $453 million high. The auctions have attracted 131 firms from around the world to bid for 20 fields and continue Friday.

The bolsa's 19-share index closed ahead 1.38 percent to end at 7,249.06 points as 33 stocks rose, seven fell and six closed flat. Trade volume meanwhile rose to a large 242 million shares, worth 9.8 billion bolivars ($20 million).

Telephone company CANTV was among the day's few losers, ending down 0.56 percent at 2675.00 bolivars. Investment bank Paribas initiated research coverage of the stock Thursday with an overvalued, sell recommendation.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes CANTV, limped ahead 0.72 percent at end at 115.02 points.
